prompt.context: Zenith Hotel is a global hotel chain with 50 hotels in 20 countries. The company is evaluating the construction of a new hotel in the Bahamas. Zenith has come to us asking whether it should and can move forward with the project.
prompt.question: Should Zenith Hotel proceed with the construction of a new hotel in the Bahamas, and can it move forward with the project?

clarifying_info.q: How many rooms will the hotel have?
What are the annual operating costs?
clarifying_info.a: The hotel would cost $20M a year to operate.

clarifying_info.q: What time horizon should we use?
clarifying_info.a: Assume that we are evaluating a ten year horizon.

clarifying_info.q: What occupancy rate should we assume?
How many days per year should we assume for the breakeven?
clarifying_info.a: Assume 350 days in a year at constant rates.

clarifying_info.q: How many visitors does the Bahamas receive?
clarifying_info.a: The Bahamas receives 50,000 visitors per month.

clarifying_info.q: How many people per room should we assume?
What is the average length of stay?
Are there regulatory or country-specific issues to consider?
clarifying_info.a: Regulatory/country-specific issues are not a concern.

framework: Internal analysis: Capabilities — does Zenith have the expertise and infrastructure to operate in the Bahamas?
Internal analysis: Start-up costs — what is the capital required to build the hotel?
Internal analysis: Expected profits — revenues (volume × price) and costs (fixed vs. variable, including insurance and marketing)
External analysis: Competition — who else operates in the Bahamas hotel market?
External analysis: Consumer demand — how many visitors come to the Bahamas and what are their willingness-to-pay characteristics?
External analysis: Regulatory/other issues — country-specific regulations (note: not a concern in this case)

questions.prompt: What is the average nightly room rate Zenith would need to charge to break even over a ten-year horizon?
questions.guidance: Candidate should sum total costs over 10 years (start-up + operating), calculate total room-nights available, and divide to find the required price per room per night.

math.setup: Total costs = start-up costs + (annual operating costs × years). Total room-nights = rooms × days per year × years. Breakeven price = total costs / total room-nights.
steps: Total room-nights = 400 rooms × 350 days/year × 10 years = 1,400,000 room-nights

questions.prompt: What is Zenith's implied market share in the Bahamas?
questions.guidance: Candidate should convert occupied rooms to visitors using occupancy rate and people-per-room, then compute monthly visitors attributed to Zenith relative to total monthly Bahamas visitors.

math.setup: Occupied rooms = total rooms × occupancy rate. Visitors at hotel at any time = occupied rooms × people per room. Monthly visitors = visitors at any time × (weeks per month), derived from 7-day average stay (1 week). Market share = Zenith monthly visitors / total monthly Bahamas visitors.
steps: Visitors at hotel at any given time = 300 rooms × 3 people/room = 900 people
With 7-day average stay, turnover is weekly; monthly visitors = 900 × 4 weeks/month = 3,600 people/month

brainstorming.prompt: Walk through the ongoing costs the hotel would incur on an ongoing basis.

categories.name: Fixed costs
ideas: Staff salaries (management, front desk, housekeeping, security)
Depreciation on the building and fixtures

categories.name: Variable costs
ideas: Food and beverage costs if hotel has restaurant

categories.name: Marketing costs
ideas: Sales force and partnerships with travel operators

recommendation: Zenith should proceed with the construction of the hotel in the Bahamas.
As a global hotel chain, capturing approximately 7% market share in the Bahamas is a reasonable and achievable goal.
risks: The breakeven analysis assumes 350 occupied days per year, which may be overly aggressive given seasonal demand patterns in the Bahamas.
Consumers' willingness to pay $500 per night must be validated against competitive pricing in the market.
next_steps: Examine consumers' willingness to pay $500/night for a Zenith hotel room in the Bahamas relative to competitive set pricing.
Stress-test occupancy assumptions with seasonal demand data to refine the breakeven calculation.
